We operate a used vehicle dealership and automotive services business in Canada. We are principally engaged in the sale of used vehicles, vehicle leasing and rental activities, and related ancillary services. Our operations are conducted through our Canadian subsidiaries, including UC Auto Limited and Carkuku Auto Ltd. We also operate certain business lines under the names Carkuku Auto Trading and UC Rental, which are business names, brands or operating divisions rather than separate legal entities. Our headquarters are located in Richmond, British Columbia, Canada, and our business is currently focused on the Greater Vancouver area. The risk factors that are material to investors in making an informed judgment have been set out below. text: We have not declared or paid any dividends on our Common Shares. We have no plan to declare or pay any dividends in the near future on our Common Shares. We currently intend to retain most, if not all, of our available funds and any future earnings to finance the operation, development and expansion of the business. Any future declaration and payment of cash dividends or other distributions of capital will be at the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend on our financial condition, results of operations, contractual restrictions, capital requirements, business prospects and any other factors that our Board deems relevant in making such a determination. UC Automotive Holdings Inc. and its subsidiaries, which we refer to as “UC Automotive,” “we,” “us,” or “our,” operate a used vehicle dealership business in Canada. We are principally engaged in the sale of used vehicles, vehicle leasing and rental activities, and related ancillary services. Our operations are conducted through our Canadian subsidiaries, including UC Auto Limited and Carkuku Auto Ltd.

Our revenue is primarily generated from auto sales, which represented substantially all of our total operating revenues for the six months ended June 30, 2026, and for the years ended December 31, 2025. We also generate revenue from car lease activities, service revenue, and other ancillary customer fees. Our business model depends on our ability to acquire desirable used vehicle inventory at competitive prices, manage inventory turnover, price vehicles effectively, and maintain sufficient gross profit after vehicle acquisition costs and other direct costs.

For the six months ended June 30, 2026, we generated total operating revenues of $22.1 million, compared with $22.4 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Although revenue decreased by approximately 1.4%, gross profit increased from $1.7 million to $1.8 million. The increase in gross profit was primarily driven by higher gross margins in both our retail and wholesale businesses, together with a greater proportion of revenue generated from our higher-margin retail business. …

sections.title: Our Corporate History and Structure
text: We were incorporated under the BCBCA on November 23, 2020 under the name “YGY Holding Ltd,” and subsequently changed our name to “UC Automotive Holdings Inc.” (“UC Holdings”). UC Auto Limited (“UC Auto”) was incorporated under the BCBCA on April 21, 2016. Carkuku Auto Ltd. (“Carkuku”) was incorporated under the BCBCA on June 11, 2021.

Prior to the reorganization described below, UC Auto and Carkuku conducted our operating business in Canada. Following the reorganization, UC Holdings became the holding company of our operating subsidiaries and owns all of the issued and outstanding equity securities of UC Auto and Carkuku.
In anticipation of this offering, we undertook a reorganization of our businesses in July and August 2026 that included the following steps.
• On July 8, 2026, YGY Holding Ltd. changed its name to “UC Automotive Holdings Inc.”
• On August 3, 2026, UC Holdings subdivided its 100 issued and outstanding common shares held by Guiyuan Yang into 9,884,625 common shares.
• On August 5, 2026, Shun Gu transferred his 1,861,000 common shares of UC Auto, representing an 18.61% ownership interest, to UC Holdings in exchange for 115,375 common shares of UC Holdings.

As a result of the reorganization, UC Auto became a wholly owned subsidiary of UC Holdings, which now owns 100% of the issued and outstanding shares of both UC Auto and Carkuku. We conduct our business through UC Auto and Carkuku.

Immediately following the reorganization and prior to this Offering, Guiyuan Yang and Shun Gu held approximately 98.85% and 1.15%, respectively, of the issued and outstanding Common Shares of UC Holdings.

sections.title: Regulations
text: Our operations are subject to extensive federal, provincial and local laws and regulations in Canada. These laws and regulations govern, among other matters, motor dealer licensing and conduct, vehicle sales, wholesale transactions, advertising, consumer protection, disclosure of the cost of credit, privacy and data protection, employment standards, occupational health and safety, anti-money laundering, competition, environmental matters, zoning, business licensing and foreign investment review. These regulatory regimes may require licences, registrations, permits, approvals, prescribed forms of agreement, mandated disclosures, recordkeeping, compliance policies and procedures, customer notices, workplace safety programs and other operational controls. Failure to obtain or maintain required licences, registrations, permits or approvals, or to comply with applicable laws and regulations, may result in investigations, administrative penalties, fines, licence suspension or revocation, civil liability, reputational harm, restrictions on business activities or other enforcement action, any of which could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects.

Our business is subject to Canadian federal, provincial and local laws and regulations that govern the sale, purchase, lease, financing and advertising of new and used motor vehicles. In British Columbia, motor dealer activities are regulated under the Motor Dealer Act (British Columbia) and related regulations. These requirements may apply to persons engaged in the business of selling motor vehicles, wholesaling motor vehicles or otherwise acting as a motor dealer, and may require applicable licences, prescribed forms of agreements, prescribed disclosures, maintenance of records, compliance with trust or security obligations and compliance with standards of conduct applicable to licensed motor dealers.

sections.title: Enforceability of Civil Liabilities
text: We are incorporated under the laws of British Columbia. Our directors and officers, and some of the experts named in this prospectus, are residents of Canada or otherwise reside outside the United States, and all or a substantial portion of their assets, and all of our assets, are located outside of the United States. We have appointed Cogency Global Inc. as our agent to receive service of process in any action against us in any U.S. federal or state court arising out of this offering or any purchase or sale of securities in connection with this offering. The address of our agent is 122 East 42nd Street, 18th Floor, New York, NY 10168. However, it may be difficult for shareholders who reside in the United States to effect service within the United States upon us or upon directors, officers and experts who are not residents of the United States. It may also be difficult for shareholders who reside in the United States to realize in the United States upon judgments of courts of the United States predicated upon our civil liability or the civil liability of our directors, officers and experts under the United States federal securities laws.

Furthermore, because substantially all of our assets and all of our directors and officers are located outside the United States, any judgment obtained in the United States against us or any of our directors and officers may not be collectible within the United States. Without an order from a court of Canada, there can be no assurance that U.S. investors will be able to enforce against us, members of our Board of Directors, officers or certain experts named herein who are residents of Canada or other countries outside the United States, any judgments of courts of the United States in civil and commercial matters, including judgments of courts of the United States under the federal securities laws.

sections.title: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements
text: Nature of business

UC Automotive Holdings Inc. (formerly known as YGY Holding Limited, “UC Automotive”) was incorporated in British Columbia, Canada on November 23, 2020. UC Automotive, through its subsidiaries (collectively, the “Company”), is principally engaged in the business of used vehicle sales and leasing in Canada.
Reorganization

In connection with the Company’s planned initial public offering, the Company completed a series of corporate reorganization transactions in July and August 2026 (the “Reorganization”). On July 8, 2026, YGY Holding Ltd. changed its name to UC Automotive Holdings Inc. On August 3, 2026, the Company subdivided its 100 issued and outstanding common shares held by Guiyuan Yang into 9,884,625 common shares. On August 5, 2026, Shun Gu transferred his 1,861,000 common shares of UC Auto, representing his 18.61% ownership interest in UC Auto, to UC Automotive in exchange for 115,375 common shares of UC Automotive.

Upon completion of the Reorganization, UC Automotive owned 100% of both of UC Auto Limited and Carkuku Auto Ltd., and Guiyuan Yang and Shun Gu held 9,884,625 and 115,375 common shares of UC Automotive, representing approximately 98.85% and 1.15%, respectively, of UC Automotive’s issued and outstanding common shares.
Basis of presentation
The consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“U.S. GAAP”).
All consolidated financial statements and notes to the consolidated financial statements are presented in United States dollars (“US Dollar” or “US$” or “$”).
Principles of consolidation

The consolidated financial statements include the financial statements of the Company and its subsidiaries. All significant intercompany transactions and balances between the Company and its subsidiaries are eliminated upon consolidation.

On August 3, 2026, the Company subdivided its 100 issued and outstanding common shares held by Guiyuan Yang into 9,884,625 common shares. On August 5, 2026, Shun Gu transferred his 1,861,000 common shares of UC Auto, representing his 18.61% ownership interest in UC Auto, to UC Automotive in exchange for 115,375 common shares of UC Automotive.

notes.title: Summary of significant accounting policies
text: Basis of presentation
The consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“U.S. GAAP”).
All consolidated financial statements and notes to the consolidated financial statements are presented in United States dollars (“US Dollar” or “US$” or “$”).
Principles of consolidation

The consolidated financial statements include the financial statements of the Company and its subsidiaries. All significant intercompany transactions and balances between the Company and its subsidiaries are eliminated upon consolidation.

Subsidiaries are those entities in which the Company, directly or indirectly, controls more than one half of the voting power; or has the power to govern the financial and operating policies, to appoint or remove the majority of the members of the board of directors, or to cast a majority of votes at the meeting of directors.

notes.title: Income taxes
text: The Company is incorporated in the province of British Columbia (“B.C.”), Canada, and is a Canadian-controlled private corporation (“CCPC”) subject to Canadian federal and B.C. provincial corporate income taxes. Taxable income differs from income before income taxes reported in the consolidated financial statements due to adjustments required under applicable Canadian tax laws.

For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, qualifying active business income up to the applicable small business limit was subject to a federal corporate income tax rate of 9% and a B.C. provincial corporate income tax rate of 2%, resulting in a combined rate of 11%. Taxable income in excess of the applicable small business limit was subject to a federal rate of 15% and a B.C. provincial rate of 12%, resulting in a combined rate of 27%. All income before income taxes for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 was generated in Canada.

notes.title: Shareholders’ equity
text: Ordinary shares

On August 3, 2026, the Company subdivided its 100 issued and outstanding common shares held by Guiyuan Yang into 9,884,625 common shares. The effect of the share subdivision has been retrospectively reflected for all periods presented. As a result, the Company has an unlimited number of authorized common shares with no par value, of which 9,884,625 shares were issued and outstanding as of December 31, 2025 and 2024.

Each Common Share entitles the holder to one vote per share to receive dividends if and when declared by the Board of Directors, and to participate equally in the distribution of the Company’s remaining assets upon liquidation, dissolution or winding-up, subject to the rights of any shares ranking in priority to the Common Shares. The Common Shares have no pre-emptive, subscription, conversion or redemption rights. All issued Common Shares are fully paid and non-assessable, and no additional capital contributions are required.

notes.title: Leases
text: The Company has several building lease agreements with lease terms ranging from two to four years. The Company adopted ASU 2016-02 on January 1, 2022. In 2023, upon commencement of its lease agreements, the Company recognized an approximately $64,097 of right of use (“ROU”) assets and operating lease liabilities based on the present value of the remaining future minimum rental payments of leases, using an incremental borrowing rate of 9.5%.

The Company’s lease agreements do not contain any material residual value guarantees or material restrictive covenants. The leases generally do not contain options to extend at the time of expiration.
As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company’s operating leases had a weighted average remaining lease term of approximately 2.18 and 3.33 years, respectively.

notes.title: Concentration of risk
text: Geographic concentration

Substantially all of the Company’s revenues are generated in Canada and substantially all of its assets are located in Canada. As a result, the Company is exposed to risks associated with changes in economic, regulatory, and market conditions in Canada.
Inventory concentration

Vehicle inventory represented approximately 47% and 52% of the Company’s total assets as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 respectively. The realizable value of inventory is subject to fluctuations in market demand, used vehicle pricing, consumer preferences, and overall economic conditions. Changes in these factors could have a material impact on the Company’s financial position and operating results.

notes.title: Subsequent events
text: On July 8, 2026, the Company changed its corporate name from YGY Holding Ltd. to UC Automotive Holdings Inc. The name change did not affect the Company’s legal structure, operations, assets, liabilities, or shareholders’ equity.

On August 5, 2026, Shun Gu transferred his 18.61% noncontrolling interest in UC Auto Limited to UC Automotive Holdings Inc. in exchange for 115,375 newly issued common shares of UC Automotive Holdings Inc. Following the transaction, UC Automotive Holdings Inc. owned 100% of UC Auto Limited, and Shun Gu held approximately 1.15% of the issued and outstanding common shares of UC Automotive Holdings Inc.

The Company has performed an evaluation of subsequent events through the date these consolidated financial statements were issued, and determined that no other event would have required adjustment or disclosure in the consolidated financial statements other than that discussed above.

revenue.heading: Revenue recognition
revenue.text: We recognize revenue from used vehicle sales, wholesale and export vehicle sales when control of the vehicle is transferred to the customer, which generally occurs upon delivery of the vehicle, transfer of title, and customer acceptance. For export sales, revenue is recognized when control transfers to the customer in accordance with the applicable contractual shipping terms. Revenue from vehicle leasing and rental arrangements is recognized in accordance with ASC 842. Ancillary fees are recognized when earned under the applicable arrangement. For sales-type and direct financing leases, the Company recognizes selling profit or loss, if applicable, at lease commencement and subsequently recognizes interest income over the lease term using the effective interest method. We continue to expand our vehicle leasing and rental operations as part of our strategy to diversify revenue sources and improve utilization of selected inventory assets.

tax.heading: Income taxes
tax.text: We account for income taxes under ASC 740. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for temporary differences between the financial statement carrying amounts and tax bases of assets and liabilities. We evaluate deferred tax assets for realizability and record a valuation allowance when it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.

ocf.heading: Operating activities
ocf.text:
Net cash used in operating activities was $489,334 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared with net cash provided by operating activities of $374,192 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Net cash used in operating activities in the first half of 2026 was primarily attributable to increases in accounts receivable and inventory, and decreases in other current liabilities and lease liabilities. These negative cash flow impacts were partially offset by net income, depreciation and amortization, and increases in accounts payable and customer deposit.

Net cash provided by operating activities was $818,311 for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared with $1.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. Net cash provided by operating activities in 2025 was primarily attributable to net income, depreciation and amortization, a reduction in inventory balances, and increases in accounts payable and other liabilities. These positive cash flow impacts were partially offset by a decrease in customer deposits and changes in other operating assets and liabilities.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text: We made capital expenditures of $9.2 thousand and $0.2 million during the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. We made capital expenditures of $0.2 million and $0.2 million during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. Capital expenditures during the periods presented primarily related to vehicles reclassified from inventory to property and equipment for use in our vehicle leasing operations, as well as leasehold improvements and equipment used to support business operations. Going forward, we expect capital expenditures to continue to support our leasing activities and operational needs.

costs.heading: Operating expenses
costs.text:
Total operating expenses increased by $551,581, or 53.6%, to $1.6 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 from $1.0 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025.

Selling expenses increased by $109,439, or 46.1%, to $347,017 for the six months ended June 30, 2026 from $237,578 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher sales and marketing-related expenses.

General and administrative expenses increased by $442,142, or 55.8%, to $1.2 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 from $791,776 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to higher personnel-related costs and accounting and legal expenses.

cor.heading: Cost of revenues
cor.text:
Cost of revenues decreased by $0.5 million, or 2.3%, to $20.3 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 from $20.8 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to lower cost of auto sales, partially offset by higher cost of other revenue.

Cost of other revenue increased by $372,803, or 93.0%, from $400,694 for the six months ended June 30, 2025 to $773,497 for the six months ended June 30, 2026. The increase was primarily attributable to higher warranty-related costs and vehicle repair and maintenance expenses. As a result, gross loss from other revenue increased by $288,355, from $162,755 to $451,110 during the respective periods.

gp.heading: Gross profit
gp.text: Gross profit increased by $167,099, or 10.0%, to $1.8 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026 from $1.7 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025. Gross margin increased to 8.3% in the first half of 2026 from 7.4% in the first half of 2025. The improvement in gross margin was primarily driven by a shift toward higher-margin retail vehicle sales, with retail vehicle sales revenue increasing to approximately 88% of total auto sales revenue in the first half of 2026 from approximately 68% in the first half of 2025, while wholesale vehicle sales revenue declined to approximately 12% from approximately 32%. The improved sales mix, together with improved vehicle purchasing and pricing and better management of direct costs, contributed to the increase in gross margin. Management believes that its continued focus on higher-margin retail vehicle sales is expected to support gross margins; however, future gross margins may be affected by changes in used vehicle market prices, vehicle acquisition costs, customer demand, and competitive pricing.

nonop.heading: Other income and expenses
nonop.text: Interest expense was $17,759 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $23,715 for the six months ended June 30, 2025, and remained relatively consistent period over period. We recognized other income, net of $28,622 for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared with other income, net of $16,032 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The change was primarily attributable to higher interest and finance income during the first half of 2026.

oi.heading: Income from operations
oi.text: Income from operations decreased by $384,482, or 60.0%, to $256,154 for the six months ended June 30, 2026 from $640,636 for the six months ended June 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to higher operating expenses, partially offset by a modest increase in gross profit.
